## Paper status

- Paper I: `SUBMISSION_READY_CANDIDATE` as a provenance-aware multi-cohort/cross-source evaluation, not a comprehensive multilingual benchmark. California RapidOCR F1 is 0.390, 0.450, 0.383, 0.428, 0.389; zero-output rates span 8%–23%. Source-agreement, authoritative-metadata, Silver, and no-GT results remain visually and inferentially separate.
- Paper II: `SUBMISSION_READY_CANDIDATE` centered on same-candidate-pool sequence reconstruction and document-level correction risk. Monotonic decoding gives v004/v005 F1 0.579/0.550; the addition-only policy accepted 82 additions in 19 documents, observed zero worsened documents, and has a one-sided 95% document-level upper bound 0.1459. The BGS external zero-coverage result remains a concise transport failure.
- Paper III: `SUBMISSION_READY_CANDIDATE` as a sensitivity diagnostic, not a complete geological-model workflow. Full-support relative volume error is raw/reread/risk 0.1387/0.1213/0.0821; on the identical 15-document subset it is 0.0326/0.0754/0.0754, showing that the apparent full-support risk gain is principally a selection/spatial-support effect.

## Boundary

Synthetic and Silver outputs are never promoted to human Gold. The authoritative
interval tier is limited to source-agreed numeric boundaries and is not described
as human annotation. The California Gold tier is explicitly a published USGS manual
transcription with published QC, not a new project annotation. Automated compliance is limited to captured licence/source
evidence and text metadata; visual privacy, sensitive-location absence, and geological correctness remain
unestablished without the corresponding evidence.
